dublinCore.description: A live spectrum analyzer for the computer's microphone with adjustable smoothness and FFT size. It shows the FFT magnitude in decibels from 0 Hz to the Nyquist frequency, the bin width, the analysis window length and the strongest peak.
relation: Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis

learningObjectives: Identify the frequency of a sustained whistle as the strongest narrow peak in the live spectrum
Calculate the bin width fs/(2N) and window length 2N/fs for a given FFT size and sample rate
Predict how raising the Smoothness slider toward 0.95 steadies the spectrum but slows its response to sudden sounds
Explain the trade-off between frequency resolution and time resolution when the FFT size changes
Compare the spectra of a whistle, a sung vowel and a hissed sss to distinguish tonal sounds from broadband noise
prerequisites: Magnitude spectrum and the decibel scale

misconceptions.misconception: A bigger FFT size shows higher frequencies
misconceptions.correction: The axis always runs from 0 Hz to the Nyquist frequency; the FFT size only changes the bin width and the window length
misconceptions.evidence: Move the FFT Size slider: the frequency axis does not change, but the bin width and window read-outs do

misconceptions.correction: Smoothness averages successive spectra over time for display; it does not change which frequencies are present
misconceptions.evidence: A steady whistle peaks at the same frequency with Smoothness 0.00 and 0.95; only the rise and fade are slower

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Live microphone spectrum analyzer. Press Start and allow microphone access; purple bars show the FFT magnitude in decibels from 0 Hz to the Nyquist frequency. The Smoothness slider averages successive spectra and the FFT Size slider sets the number of frequency bins.

controls.label: Start / Stop
controls.description: Opens or closes the microphone; the sound is analyzed locally and never played back

controls.label: Reset
controls.description: Restores Smoothness 0.50 and FFT Size 1024 bins

controls.label: Smoothness
controls.description: Averaging constant applied to successive spectra (the analyser's smoothingTimeConstant)

controls.label: FFT Size (bins)
controls.description: Index into 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384 frequency bins; a new p5.FFT is built for each size

visualElements.description: Purple bars: FFT magnitude in dB (-100 to -30) versus frequency from 0 Hz to the Nyquist frequency, with a gold marker on the strongest peak
Sample rate, bin width, window length, strongest peak, cursor frequency and microphone status

model.description: A Web Audio analyser (Blackman window, 2N-sample FFT, N bins) applied to the live microphone signal, smoothed over time and displayed in decibels

instructionalStrategies: Predict the effect of FFT size, then check with a steady whistle
extensions: Add a frequency-range zoom or a log-frequency axis
